[TGT] Ram Wrangler and 2 class legendaries: Rhonin and Varian Wrynn

Holy value! Varian Wrynn will probably be included in wallet warrior along with many other value-oriented cards in this expansion and make the deck even better than it currently is. Even if you don't draw any minions with him, if you consider draw 3 cards to be worth 5 mana (Nourish and Lay on Hands (where Lay on Hands also includes a 3 mana Healing Touch)), you're already getting a 5 mana 7/7. Add the fact that you get any minions directly played makes it insane! If, for example, on average you'll get a 3-4 mana minion and 2 spells (random numbers), you're paying 6-7 mana for a 7/7 that draws 2 cards.
That being said, you'll lose value on Battlecry cards, including BGH, Harrison Jones, Cruel Taskmaster.

Also good to see Hunter cards that are more value than face (although Ram Wrangler does still require board presence and grants tempo, so it's still a midrangey tempo card).

Rhonin seems to fit nicely into several existing Mage archetypes, including Tempo Mage and any deck that has Antonidas as a win condition (Freeze Mage, Spare Parts/Mech Mage). With 3 Thaurissan-ed Arcane Missles, That's 24 missiles for 0 mana with a Malygos, too!

The beta API was developed as part of the UI code. Since Voat's growth we can no longer run the API along with the site on the same servers. API has to be stripped out and function on it's own. Study was done by Harry Harlow. It was indeed very strange and is believed to have launched a slew of research-animal liberation movements.

They basically took baby monkeys from their mothers at a very young age and placed them in an isolation cage with 2 "artificial mothers". One of the artificial mothers was made of wire and provided milk while the other was covered in snuggly fur but did not provide food. Then they proceeded to scare the shit out of the monkeys and see which one they ran to.

Unsurprisingly they virtually all ran to the snuggly monkey mother. Which was actually pretty adorable...
Yup but we learned quite a bit about human behaviors. Science has done some cruel things in the past but we still learned something from it.

It's from an interesting but somewhat inhumane study.

Basically, they wanted to test whether primates bond to comfort or nourishment.

On the left is "wire mother," which provided the baby monkey with milk. On the right is "cloth mother," which provided no nourishment but was wrapped in a blanket.

The result? Essentially, primates bond to the thing that is more snuggly, not the thing that provides nourishment.
